alt: The CouchCrew home page after John's polish, styled as a cinema lobby: a lit marquee sign, a box office with a Buy a Ticket button, a concessions stand with popcorn, soda and candy, and a Theater 1 entrance where you type a room code and press Join.
caption: The home page now. One ticket makes a room and its link is what you send; the entrance on the right joins one by code. The cinema look is John's polish pass.

alt: A new CouchCrew room in the cinema theme: a movie screen showing a film countdown, with a Join call button and Mic on and Camera on checkboxes under it, a YouTube link field with a Load button below that, and rows of red seats in front.
caption: Inside a new room: the screen waits for a video, and under it the video call (my part) starts when you press Join call, with mic and camera optional. Only the room leader chooses what plays.

alt: A CouchCrew room. A YouTube video is playing at the top. Below it the call shows three tiles: Henry on camera, a plain letter A for Adrian, who has no webcam, and John on camera, with In the call: 3 under them and Mute, Camera off, Share screen and Leave call buttons. The chat panel is open on the right with joined and left messages and lines from Adrian, John and Henry.
caption: The test that counted: three of us, each on a different network, in one call on our own peer-to-peer version, with the video playing above and chat open. Adrian has no webcam, so he shows as a letter and watched and listened.

alt: A CouchCrew room on a narrow screen. The Watch Together box shows a YouTube message reading Sign in to confirm you're not a bot. Below it the video call shows three tiles: Adrian as a blue letter A, Henry in front of a world map, and John in front of a window.
caption: The first real test of the Jitsi version, with all three of us in one room. The call worked. The YouTube player did not: it asked us to sign in to prove we were not bots.
